from Cocoa import *
from PyObjCTools import AppHelper

def click_button_in_simulator():
    # Find and interact with the iOS Simulator
    workspace = NSWorkspace.sharedWorkspace()
    
    # Find the Simulator app
    for running_app in workspace.runningApplications():
        app_name = running_app.localizedName()
        print(f"Found app: {app_name}")
        
        if "Simulator" in app_name or "iOS" in app_name:
            print(f"Found iOS Simulator: {app_name}")
            pid = running_app.processIdentifier()
            
            # Create accessibility element from the app
            app_element = AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)
            
            # Get the main window
            windows = NSMutableArray.array()
            AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue(app_element, kAXWindowsAttribute, windows)
            
            if windows.count() > 0:
                window = windows.objectAtIndex_(0)
                
                # Find the Open button by searching for buttons
                buttons = NSMutableArray.array()
                AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue(window, kAXButtonsAttribute, buttons)
                
                for i in range(buttons.count()):
                    button = buttons.objectAtIndex_(i)
                    title = NSMutableValue.valueWithBytes_(None, "@")
                    AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue(button, kAXTitleAttribute, title)
                    print(f"Found button: {title.objCValue if title else 'Unknown'}")
                    
                    # Check if this is the Open button
                    if title and "Open" in str(title.objCValue):
                        print("Clicking Open button...")
                        AXUIElementPerformAction(button, kAXPressAction)
                        return True
    
    return False

click_button_in_simulator()
EOF

python3 << 'EOF'
from pynput.mouse import Controller, Button
from pynput.keyboard import Controller as KeyController, Key
import subprocess
import time

mouse = Controller()
keyboard = KeyController()

# Take a screenshot first
subprocess.run(["xcrun", "simctl", "io", "67FE35B5-EF24-4552-86B7-2C9E44640D03", 
                "screenshot", "/tmp/pre_click.png"], check=True)

# Estimate the Simulator window position
# Typical MacBook Pro: 2560x1600
# Simulator window (iPhone vertical): ~540px wide, ~1080px tall
# If centered: x = 2560/2 = 1280, y = 1600/2 = 800
# Or shifted: x = 1280 - 270 = 1010 (left of center), y = similar

# The Weekend Plans room row is at about 710px in the simulator
# That's about 2/3 down the screen
# So screen y would be: 800 + (710 * 1080 / 2340) ≈ 1125

# But let me also try several other position estimates
# in case the window is positioned differently

print("Attempting systematic mouse clicks...")

attempt_positions = [
    # Center of typical MacBook screen
    (1280, 1000),  # Rough center
    (1280, 1100),  # Lower
    (1280, 1200),  # Even lower
    
    # Off-center positions (window might be on side)
    (800, 1100),   # Left side
    (1600, 1100),  # Right side
    
    # Different screen size estimates
    (640, 550),    # Smaller display
    (960, 825),    # Medium display
    (1440, 1100),  # Larger display
]

for i, (x, y) in enumerate(attempt_positions):
    print(f"\nAttempt {i+1}: Clicking at ({x}, {y})...")
    
    # Move and click
    mouse.position = (x, y)
    time.sleep(0.2)
    mouse.click(Button.left, 1)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    
    # Take a screenshot to check
    subprocess.run(["xcrun", "simctl", "io", "67FE35B5-EF24-4552-86B7-2C9E44640D03",
                     "screenshot", f"/tmp/click_test_{i}.png"],
                   stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)

# Take a final screenshot to see current state
subprocess.run(["xcrun", "simctl", "io", "67FE35B5-EF24-4552-86B7-2C9E44640D03",
                 "screenshot", "/tmp/final_state.png"], check=True)

print("\nFinal screenshot saved to /tmp/final_state.png")
EOF
